beforeReference.supportingExcerpt: Recognition differs by subset, and it is not always free of HLA. For the Vγ9Vδ2 subset, which responds to phosphoantigens (small phosphorylated metabolites produced by microbes and overexpressed by some cancers), butyrophilin 2A1 (BTN2A1) binds the Vγ9 chain of the receptor, associates with a second butyrophilin, BTN3A1, and the two act together to start the response; a second ligand, possibly BTN3A1, binds a separate region that includes the Vδ2 chain (Rigau et al., 2020). This is not a peptide sitting in an HLA groove. HLA independence is also not universal: one characterised Vγ5Vδ1 receptor was restricted by HLA-A*24:02 and depended on the CD8-alpha co-receptor, acting on blood-cancer and solid-tumour cells in vitro and in vivo while sparing healthy tissue in those models (Kierkels et al., 2019). That receptor's mechanism is not an eligibility rule for the family.

beforeReference.supportingExcerpt: For interpretation, report the parent population, percentage and any valid absolute count with the specimen and sampling method. Receptor-sequence abundance does not identify the receptor ligand. Rigau et al. (2020) established a defined BTN2A1-dependent recognition mechanism for the Vgamma9Vdelta2 phosphoantigen response; that specificity is an example of why innate-like does not mean nonspecific. To test native versus added-receptor recognition, compare matched cells without the added receptor, target-positive and target-negative cells, and a suitable receptor-blocking or target-perturbation condition. Keep relevant healthy-cell controls, viability and exposure conditions explicit. This is experimental-design reasoning from the separate recognition mechanisms, not a claim that one cited assay validates every product. HLA loss does not establish that the native ligand or the added receptor target is present, and two recognition routes do not prove escape prevention.

beforeReference.supportingExcerpt: An engineered receptor is a separate recognition route. Adding a GD2-directed chimeric antigen receptor to expanded human Vδ1 and Vδ2 cells increased GD2-specific killing of GD2-expressing cancer cell lines, did not impair movement towards tumour cells in vitro, and expanded Vδ2 cells kept the ability to take up tumour antigen and cross-present it to alpha-beta T cells (Capsomidis et al., 2018). That is a preclinical result for that preparation, and it does not show that any gamma-delta product enters tumours, cross-presents usefully or prevents antigen escape in patients. An allogeneic gamma-delta product that the registry names HLA-G-CAR.BiTE allogeneic γδ T cells (NCT06150885, phase 1 and 2) was listed as recruiting when the registry record was read for this entry; the record describes the product and the study design and reports no efficacy. A receptor added to a cell needs its own target on the tumour, HLA-low does not mean target-positive, and avoiding peptide presentation is not the same as avoiding antigen escape. Cells are identified by flow cytometry and receptor sequencing, but a response against one target line does not establish tumour entry, persistence or benefit, and matched cells without the added receptor are needed to separate native from engineered recognition. Two cautions are OnCo's reasoning and not findings of the cited papers: a product made of many receptor clones is not automatically broader or more effective than one defined clone, and the name gamma-delta describes the receptor chains and not the cell source, so whether cells came from the patient or from a donor has to be stated separately.

beforeReference.supportingExcerpt: Recognition differs by subset, and it is not always free of HLA. For the Vγ9Vδ2 subset, which responds to phosphoantigens (small phosphorylated metabolites produced by microbes and overexpressed by some cancers), butyrophilin 2A1 (BTN2A1) binds the Vγ9 chain of the receptor, associates with a second butyrophilin, BTN3A1, and the two act together to start the response; a second ligand, possibly BTN3A1, binds a separate region that includes the Vδ2 chain (Rigau et al., 2020). This is not a peptide sitting in an HLA groove. HLA independence is also not universal: one characterised Vγ5Vδ1 receptor was restricted by HLA-A*24:02 and depended on the CD8-alpha co-receptor, acting on blood-cancer and solid-tumour cells in vitro and in vivo while sparing healthy tissue in those models (Kierkels et al., 2019). That receptor's mechanism is not an eligibility rule for the family.

beforeReference.supportingExcerpt: An engineered receptor is a separate recognition route. Adding a GD2-directed chimeric antigen receptor to expanded human Vδ1 and Vδ2 cells increased GD2-specific killing of GD2-expressing cancer cell lines, did not impair movement towards tumour cells in vitro, and expanded Vδ2 cells kept the ability to take up tumour antigen and cross-present it to alpha-beta T cells (Capsomidis et al., 2018). That is a preclinical result for that preparation, and it does not show that any gamma-delta product enters tumours, cross-presents usefully or prevents antigen escape in patients. An allogeneic gamma-delta product that the registry names HLA-G-CAR.BiTE allogeneic γδ T cells (NCT06150885, phase 1 and 2) was listed as recruiting when the registry record was read for this entry; the record describes the product and the study design and reports no efficacy. A receptor added to a cell needs its own target on the tumour, HLA-low does not mean target-positive, and avoiding peptide presentation is not the same as avoiding antigen escape. Cells are identified by flow cytometry and receptor sequencing, but a response against one target line does not establish tumour entry, persistence or benefit, and matched cells without the added receptor are needed to separate native from engineered recognition. Two cautions are OnCo's reasoning and not findings of the cited papers: a product made of many receptor clones is not automatically broader or more effective than one defined clone, and the name gamma-delta describes the receptor chains and not the cell source, so whether cells came from the patient or from a donor has to be stated separately.

beforeReference.supportingExcerpt: For interpretation, report the parent population, percentage and any valid absolute count with the specimen and sampling method.
